examples.en: The government reforms the education system.
They picked a new head to reform the company.
We reformed the old way, and work got faster.
After the reform, the students liked it.
I want to reform this rule.
We have to decide what to reform first.

explain: 제도, 조직, 규칙 같은 큰 것을 근본부터 바꾼다는 말이에요. 작은 물건이나 습관은 '고치다', '바꾸다'를 써요. 뉴스에서는 '개혁'이라는 명사 모양으로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means changing something big, such as a system, organization or rule, from its foundations. For small objects or habits use '고치다' or '바꾸다'. In the news it often appears as the noun '개혁'.

examples.en: France is a republic without a king.
In a republic, an elected person leads the country.
India became a republic in 1950.
People gathered to found a new republic.
Korea is also a republic, so we elect a president.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 로마 공화국에 대해 배웠어요.
examples.en: We learned about the Roman Republic in history class.

explain: '공화국'은 나라 이름이나 정치 제도를 말할 때 나와요. '대한민국은 민주공화국이다'라는 문장이 헌법에도 있어요. 짝이 되는 말로 '왕국'을 써요.
explain_en: It appears in country names and when talking about political systems. The sentence '대한민국은 민주공화국이다' is in the constitution. The contrasting word is '왕국' (kingdom).

examples.en: This work is related to my major.
I saw news related to the accident.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 이 일과 관련되지 않았어요.
examples.en: That person isn't connected to this matter.
This document is related to taxes.
Please bring all the relevant documents.

examples.ko: 두 사건이 서로 관련됐을 수도 있어요.
examples.en: The two incidents may be related to each other.

explain: 'A와 관련되다' 또는 'A에 관련되다'로 써요. '관련이 있다'와 뜻이 가까운데, '관련되다'는 앞에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 '관련된 자료'처럼 자주 써요. 뉴스와 회사 말에서 흔해요.
explain_en: Used as 'A와 관련되다' or 'A에 관련되다' (be related to A). It is close to '관련이 있다', but 관련되다 is especially common as a modifier, as in '관련된 자료'. It is frequent in news and workplace language.

p.n: 연관되다 stresses a link in a chain of connection.

examples.en: The United States has a vice president as well as a president.
The vice president works to assist the president.
The people elected a new vice president.
The vice president's speech was shown on TV.
On the news, the vice president held a press conference.
A reporter asked the vice president a question.

explain: 지금 한국에는 부통령이 없어요. 대신 '국무총리'라는 자리가 있어요. 그래서 이 말은 미국 같은 다른 나라 뉴스에서 주로 나와요.
explain_en: Korea currently has no vice president. It has a '국무총리' (prime minister) instead. So this word mostly appears in news about other countries such as the U.S.

examples.en: Korea has existed as a divided country for a long time.

examples.ko: 분단국가에 사는 사람들은 통일에 관심이 많아요.
examples.en: People living in a divided country are very interested in reunification.
In history class we learned about examples of divided countries.
Germany was also once a divided country.
The fact that it is a divided country is often mentioned in the news.

examples.ko: 외국인 친구가 분단국가에서의 생활이 궁금하다고 했어요.
examples.en: A foreign friend said they were curious about life in a divided country.

explain: 한 나라가 정치적인 이유로 둘 이상으로 나뉜 상태의 나라를 말해요. 한국 이야기를 할 때 자주 나와요. 짝이 되는 말은 '통일'이에요.
explain_en: It refers to a country split into two or more parts for political reasons. It comes up often when talking about Korea. Its counterpart is '통일' (unification).

en: law of the jungle; the weak becoming prey to the strong

examples.en: In the animal world, the strong preying on the weak is the basic rule.

examples.ko: 회사에서 약육강식의 논리만 따르면 팀워크가 깨져요.
examples.en: If a company only follows the law of the jungle, teamwork breaks down.

examples.ko: 약육강식 사회에서는 약한 사람이 살아가기 힘들어요.
examples.en: In a dog-eat-dog society, it's hard for weak people to get by.
As the phrase 'law of the jungle' says, competition in the market is fierce.

examples.ko: 우리는 약육강식을 넘어서 서로 돕는 사회를 원해요.
examples.en: We want a society that goes beyond the law of the jungle and helps one another.

examples.ko: 약육강식에서 벗어나 공존하는 방법을 배워야 해요.
examples.en: We need to learn how to break away from the law of the jungle and coexist.

explain: 동물의 세계뿐 아니라 경쟁이 심하고 강한 쪽이 이기는 사회를 비유할 때도 자주 써요. '정글의 법칙'과 비슷한 느낌이고, 보통 그런 상황을 비판하거나 걱정하는 말투로 나와요. 사자성어라서 글이나 토론에서 많이 보여요.
explain_en: Besides the animal world, it is often used as a metaphor for a fiercely competitive society where the strong win. It feels similar to 'the law of the jungle' and usually appears when criticizing or worrying about such a situation. As a four-character idiom, it is common in writing and debates.

examples.en: This issue is directly tied to our daily lives.
I think sleep time is directly tied to grades.

examples.ko: 안전과 직결된 일이라서 더 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: It is work tied directly to safety, so we have to be more careful.
Don't put off problems that bear directly on your health.

examples.ko: 이 지하철역은 백화점과 바로 직결되어 있어요.
examples.en: This subway station is directly connected to the department store.

examples.ko: 그 발표가 회사의 미래와 직결될 거예요.
examples.en: That announcement will be directly tied to the company's future.

explain: '~와 직결되다'처럼 조사 '와/과'와 같이 쓰는 일이 많아요. 중간 단계 없이 바로 영향을 준다는 느낌이라서 안전·건강·생활 같은 말과 자주 붙어요. 지하철역과 건물이 이어졌을 때처럼 실제 통로에도 써요.
explain_en: It is often used with the particle 와/과, as in ~와 직결되다. It feels like something affects another with no step in between, so it often goes with words like safety, health, and daily life. It also works for physical links such as a subway station joined to a building.

examples.en: A big bear suddenly appeared in the forest.

examples.ko: 새로운 스타가 출현해서 인기를 끌고 있어요.
examples.en: A new star has emerged and is gaining popularity.
Wild boars often show up in this area.

examples.ko: 휴대폰이 출현한 뒤로 생활이 많이 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: Life changed a lot after cell phones appeared.
I'm worried that a rival might appear.

examples.ko: 공룡이 출현하는 영화를 아이와 같이 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a movie with dinosaurs in it together with my child.

explain: 출현하다는 없던 것이나 예상 못 한 것이 눈앞에 나타날 때 써요. 동물, 새 인물, 새 기술처럼 갑자기 등장하는 대상에 잘 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '나타나다'를 훨씬 많이 쓰고 출현하다는 뉴스나 글에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: 출현하다 is used when something that was not there, or was unexpected, appears. It fits animals, new people, or new technology showing up suddenly. In daily talk '나타나다' is far more common, while 출현하다 appears more in news and writing.

p.n: 출현하다 sounds formal, like news; 나타나다 is the everyday word.

en: to seize; to take advantage of

examples.en: A thief took advantage of the dark and broke into the shop.
I used the lunch break to run to the bank.

examples.ko: 불안한 마음을 틈타는 사기가 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: Scams that prey on people's anxiety are increasing.

examples.ko: 아이들이 어른이 바쁜 사이를 틈타 과자를 꺼내 먹었어요.
examples.en: While the adults were busy, the kids sneaked out snacks to eat.

examples.ko: 바쁜 시기를 틈타지 말고 정직하게 팔아야 해요.
examples.en: You shouldn't exploit the busy season; you have to sell honestly.

examples.ko: 출근길 짬을 틈타 영어 단어를 외워요.
examples.en: I memorize English words in the spare moments on my commute.

explain: '틈을 타다'처럼 띄어 써도 같은 뜻이에요. 범죄나 사기처럼 나쁜 일에 쓰기도 하고, 짧은 여유 시간을 잘 활용한다는 좋은 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: It means the same when written separately as '틈을 타다'. It can be used for bad things like crime and scams, and also in a positive sense of making good use of a short free moment.
